# Local modifications to vendored sources

Every edit is marked in the source with `PATCH (omgui-mac)`. Baseline commits are in each
directory's `UPSTREAM.md`. Nothing outside this list was changed.

Verification: each file compiles with `clang -c -arch arm64 -Wall -I Vendor/libomapi/include`
with **zero warnings and zero errors** on Xcode 26.6 / macOS 26.6 (arm64).

Rows tagged **C\<n\>** implement the correspondingly numbered confirmed finding in
`refs/10-deep-review.md`; rows tagged **H\<n\>/M\<n\>/L\<n\>/U\<n\>** implement one from the
second review, `refs/12-deep-review-2.md`.

The C3/C6/C17 rows below are **superseded**: H1-H4 found that the first fix pass moved the
use-after-free rather than closing it. The shutdown/removal design that replaces them is one thing,
not four patches, and is described once under `omapi-download.c` row 1; `refs/13-fixes2-libomapi.md`
records what it does not cover.

## `libomapi/include/omapi.h`

| # | What | Why |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `typedef unsigned long OM_DATETIME;` → `typedef uint32_t OM_DATETIME;` (plus `#include <stdint.h>`) | **Correctness bug on any LP64 build.** `unsigned long` is 32-bit on Windows, where this library was written and where the C# binding declares the same values as `uint`, but 64-bit on macOS. `OM_DATETIME` is a member of the tightly-packed `OM_READER_HEADER_PACKET` / `OM_READER_DATA_PACKET`, whose own comments document it as 4 bytes. Measured on macOS 26 / arm64 before the change: `sizeof(OM_READER_DATA_PACKET)` was **516** (not 512) and every field after `timestamp` was shifted by +4 — `light@22` (should be 18), `temperature@24` (20), `events@26` (22), `battery@27` (23), `sampleRate@28` (24), `numAxesBPS@29` (25), `timestampOffset@30` (26), `sampleCount@32` (28), `rawSampleData@34` (30), `checksum@514` (510, i.e. past the end of the 512-byte buffer). `OM_READER_HEADER_PACKET` was 1032 with `annotation@72` instead of 1024/`@64`. Consequence: `OmReaderGetValue()` returned garbage for `OM_VALUE_LIGHT`, `_TEMPERATURE`, `_EVENTS`, `_BATTERY`, `_SAMPLERATE` and all the cooked `_MC` / `_MV` / `_PERCENT` variants — exactly the values `omapinet`'s `OmReader.ReadBlock()` exposes and OMGUI's DataViewer plots. After the change all offsets match `Docs/ax3/cwa.h` exactly. `OM_DATETIME_INFINITE` becomes `0xFFFFFFFF`, which is still `> OM_DATETIME_MAX_VALID` (`0xFF3F7EFB`), so the `HIBERNATE`/`STOP` sentinel handling in `omapi-settings.c` is unchanged. Guarded by `Tests/OmApiTests/COmApiLayoutTests.swift`. |

## `libomapi/src/omapi-devicefinder-mac.c`

| # | What | Why |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `kIOMasterPortDefault` → `kIOMainPortDefault` (2 sites: `findSerial`, `IONotificationPortCreate`) | Deprecated in macOS 12; the only deprecation warning the file produced. |
| 2 | `findMount()` rewritten | Upstream recovered the volume *name* by string-scanning `CFCopyDescription()` output (including a stray `if (isdigit(*p)) *p = 'x';` that corrupts any name starting with a digit), assumed the mount point was `/Volumes/<name>`, and assumed the data partition was always `<disk>s1`. A volume name is not a mount point (the mounter appends ` 1` on collision, and names may contain `/`); some units present a "superfloppy" with no partition table, so the volume is the whole disk; and the AX6 does not use the `AX317_` label the file's header comment assumed. The replacement asks DiskArbitration for the real mount path (`kDADiskDescriptionVolumePathKey` → `CFURLGetFileSystemRepresentation`), tries the whole disk plus partitions 1–4, and **selects the volume by the presence of `CWA-DATA.CWA`** — label-independent, so AX3 and AX6 are handled identically. A mounted volume without the data file is accepted only after ~3 s of polling, with a warning (covers the window just after a `FORMAT`). It also releases the `CFStringRef`/`DADiskRef`/`CFDictionaryRef` upstream leaked on every call, and polls `om.quitDiscoveryThread` so shutdown is not blocked. Total wait dropped from up to 22 s to ~8 s. |
| 3 | Added `volumeHasDataFile()` and `mountPathForBsdName()` helpers; added `<ctype.h>` and `<sys/stat.h>` | Support for #2. `isdigit()` was already used in the file with no `<ctype.h>` include. |
| 4 | Removed `cfTypeToCString()` and `cfStringRefToCString()` | Only callers were in the replaced `findMount()`. |
| 5 | Removed `osVersion()`; `serviceMatcher` fixed to `"IOUSBHostDevice"` | `osVersion()` mapped Darwin→macOS as `major - 9`, which was right up to macOS 15 (Darwin 24) and is wrong from macOS 26 (Darwin 25). It only gated an El-Capitan-era `IOUSBDevice`/`IOUSBHostDevice` choice; this build targets macOS 14+, where the class is always `IOUSBHostDevice`. (The stale value happened not to change the outcome, but it is a live landmine.) |
| 6 | Removed the `SIGINT` handler that called `exit(0)` | A library must not take over the host app's Ctrl-C, and must never exit the process on its behalf. Fatal for a GUI app. |
| 7 | `OmDeviceDiscoveryStop()`: `CFRunLoopStop` + `thread_join` instead of `CFRunLoopStop` + `pthread_cancel`; `gRunLoop` NULL-guarded and cleared | `pthread_cancel` immediately after `CFRunLoopStop` can tear the thread down inside CoreFoundation. Joining is now safe because the rewritten `findMount()` observes `om.quitDiscoveryThread`. |
| 8 | `DeviceIdFromSerialNumber()` returns `0` (was `(unsigned int)-1`) when the serial has no digits; caller's test `<= 0` → `== 0` | On an `unsigned int` the caller's `<= 0` could only ever be true for `0`, so the "no device id" path was dead. |
| 9 | Dropped an unused `kern_return_t kr` in `DeviceNotification()` | Silences `-Wunused-but-set-variable`; the two `IOObjectRelease`/`Release` results were never checked. |

| 10 | **C14** `getUSBStringDescriptor()`: reject `wLenDone < 2`, clamp the character count to what `buffer`/the allocation hold, check the `malloc` | `count = (request.wLenDone - 1) / 2` is unsigned arithmetic: a device that ACKs the control transfer with a zero-length string descriptor (a re-enumerating AX3 straight after a `FORMAT`) wrapped it to `0x7FFFFFFF`, and the copy loop then wrote 2.1 GB into a 128-byte heap buffer. |
| 11 | **C6**, extended by **L1** `DeviceAdded()`: `IOServiceAddInterestNotification()` moved to after every lookup has succeeded; the release epilogue (notification / `deviceName` / device interface / the three heap strings) factored into `DeviceDataRelease()` and shared by the failure path, `DeviceNotification()` and `Stop()`; the record registered on `gDeviceDataList` once it is owned by the armed notification | Upstream armed the `kIOGeneralInterest` notification with `deviceData` as its refCon *before* four steps that can `break` (`getUSBSerialNumber`, `DeviceIdFromSerialNumber`, `findMount`, `findSerial`), then `free()`d the struct bare — leaving a live notification on a dangling pointer. On the eventual unplug `DeviceNotification()` read freed memory and passed garbage `%s` pointers into `OmDeviceDiscovery(OM_DEVICE_REMOVED, ...)`. `findMount()` gives up after ~8 s, so this was reachable just by attaching a unit still re-mounting after a `FORMAT`, or one waiting on "Allow accessory to connect". |
| 12 | **C36** `DeviceNotification()`: free `serialNumber`, `mountPath` and `serialDevice` | ~1.2 KB leaked per attach/detach cycle, unbounded, on the app's hot path. (The first two were previously recorded here as known findings; `mountPath` was introduced by row 2.) |
| 13 | **C17** `OmDeviceDiscoveryStart()`/`Stop()`: `gStarted` is now signalled from a `CFRunLoopPerformBlock` running *inside* the loop (the 200 ms "HACK" delay is gone), the thread also signals on every exit path, and `Stop()` retries `CFRunLoopStop()` for up to ~5 s against a `gFinished` condition variable before joining | The old signal fired *before* `CFRunLoopRun()`, so a quick quit — which `--self-test` performs by construction — could issue its `CFRunLoopStop()` into a loop that had not started and then block forever in an unbounded `thread_join` on Cmd-Q. **Superseded in part by rows 14–16**: C17's *detach* path and its release order were themselves unsafe. |
| 14 | **H4** `Stop()`'s detach path: null `om.deviceCallback`, `om.downloadCallback`, `om.downloadChunkCallback` and `om.logCallback` (with their references), clear `gRunLoop`, set `gDiscoveryDetached`, and only then `pthread_detach()`; `gNotifyPort`, `gAddedIter` and the `DeviceData` registry are left to the orphan | C17 traded a hang for undefined behaviour: it detached the thread and told `OmShutdown()` nothing, so the frees and both `mutex_destroy()`s ran while a thread stuck >5 s in `getUSBStringDescriptor()`'s `DeviceRequest` or in a DiskArbitration call was still walking the device table, locking `om.downloadMutex`, and calling `om.deviceCallback` — which resolves an `Unmanaged<LibOmapiBackend>` the caller nulls only *after* `OmShutdown()` returns. Cutting every route back into the caller first, and telling `OmShutdown()` to free and destroy nothing (`OmDeviceDiscoveryDetached()`), makes a wedged quit a deliberate leak instead. Destroying the port under the orphan would be the same crash, so the orphan keeps it. |
| 15 | **M1** `gStartMutex`/`gStartCond` are `PTHREAD_MUTEX_INITIALIZER`/`PTHREAD_COND_INITIALIZER` and never re-initialised or destroyed; `gStarted`/`gFinished` are reset *under* the lock; `Start()` refuses to run at all once `gDiscoveryDetached` is set | C17 re-ran `pthread_mutex_init()`/`pthread_cond_init()` on the same statics at the top of every `Start()` — undefined on an already-initialised mutex, and worse after an H4 detach, where an orphan is still locking it from `OmDiscoverySignal()`. Those are single global slots, so an orphan signalling `(1,1)` on a *new* cycle's globals made the new `Start()` return before its run loop was up and the next `Stop()` skip every `CFRunLoopStop()` and then join a running loop — a permanent hang, i.e. the exact bug C17 exists to remove. The review's per-run heap context would also work; refusing to restart discovery after an orphaned stop is the review's own fallback and is what a wedged quit actually needs. |
| 16 | **L1** every `DeviceData` is chained on `gDeviceDataList` and released by `Stop()` — running `DeviceNotification()`'s own epilogue — before `gAddedIter` and `gNotifyPort` go; unchanged on the H4 detach path | A `DeviceData` is owned by its armed `kIOGeneralInterest` notification and released only inside `DeviceNotification()`, which can never fire once the port is destroyed. Every stop/start cycle therefore leaked one `DeviceData` plus the ~1.2 KB of strings C36 added frees for, per attached device. `Stop()` walks the list only after `thread_join()`, so no lock is needed; no `OM_DEVICE_REMOVED` is issued, because the devices are still attached and a restart's `DeviceAdded()` reports them again. |

Upstream findings now fixed by rows 10–12 and 16 (previously recorded here as known leaks, see
`refs/04-phase1-notes.md`): the unfreed `getUSBStringDescriptor()`/`findSerial()` strings, and the
`deviceName` leak on the mid-enumeration failure path.

## `libomapi/src/omapi-internal.h`

| # | What | Why |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **C15** `OmDeviceState.deviceStatus`, `OmDeviceRecord.state` and `OmState.deviceRecords` are `_Atomic` (`#include <stdatomic.h>`) | The device table is published by the discovery thread and walked, unlocked, by the caller's thread — in OmGui a 100 ms tick on the main thread. The plain store of the list head had no release barrier, so on arm64 a reader could see the new head before the record's own fields, i.e. a record whose `state`/`next` is still pre-`memset` garbage. Qualifying the three fields that cross the boundary makes every existing access a (sequentially consistent) atomic one *without changing a single access site*; records are never removed from the list, and `deviceStatus` is the last field written on connect, so a reader that sees `OM_DEVICE_CONNECTED` also sees the `port`/`root`/`serialId` written before it. |
| 2 | **C3**, superseded by **H1/H3** Declares the download lifecycle split: `OmDownloadStartThread()`, `OmDownloadRequestCancel()`, `OmDownloadWaitFinished()`, `OmDownloadJoinBounded()` and `OM_DOWNLOAD_JOIN_TIMEOUT_MS`. `OmDownloadCancelJoin()` is kept as a compatibility spelling of request+reap. Also declares `OmDeviceDiscoveryDetached()` (H4) and the `OmTest*` hooks | See `omapi-download.c` row 1. |
| 3 | **H1/H3** `OmDeviceState` gains `downloadFinished` and `downloadThreadActive`, and `downloadCancel` becomes `_Atomic char` (was `volatile char`); `thread_detach` added to the thread macros | `downloadCancel` is read by the download thread with no lock held, which `volatile` does not make a race-free read; it is now written under `om.downloadMutex`, the same critical section that invalidates `downloadSource`. `downloadFinished` is the thread's promise that it has stopped touching the structure — the whole shutdown design is built on it. `downloadThreadActive` means "a thread exists that has not published `downloadFinished`", so a reap after a detach still refuses to declare the state free-able. |

## `libomapi/src/omapi-internal.c`

| # | What | Why |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `OmPortOpen()` (non-Windows): `if (infile == NULL && infile[0] == '\0')` → `\|\|` | The `&&` form dereferences `infile` after establishing it is `NULL`. Unreachable today (callers pass a `char[]` field), but it is a NULL dereference as written. |
| 2 | **C3**, superseded by **H1/H2** `OmDeviceDiscovery(OM_DEVICE_REMOVED)`: store `deviceStatus = OM_DEVICE_REMOVED` **first**, then `OmDownloadRequestCancel()`. No join here at all | Upstream never joined (its `OmCancelDownload()` was refused by `OmQueryDownload()`'s CONNECTED check), so every unplug-during-download orphaned a thread still `fread()`ing the dying volume. C3 fixed that with an *unbounded* join — on the IOKit run-loop thread, which is worse: while it blocks, no attach/detach notification is delivered and no `CFRunLoopStop()` is processed, so Cmd-Q could not stop discovery, `OmDeviceDiscoveryStop()`'s bounded wait gave up, and `free()` ran under two live threads. C3 also put the join *ahead* of the status store, leaving the device readable as CONNECTED for the length of a download: `OmBeginDownloading()`'s "device lost" guard still passed, the main thread cleared `downloadCancel` and created a fresh thread, and the run-loop thread ended up waiting for a full download off a disappearing volume. `deviceStatus` is `_Atomic`, so storing REMOVED first closes that window immediately; the thread is reaped by whoever comes next (`OmShutdown()`, or the device's next `OmBeginDownloading()`). |
| 3 | **C15** `deviceState->id`/`port`/`root`/`serialId` are filled in before the record is linked into the table; `deviceStatus` stays the last write | A record must never be visible to the reader thread pointing at a half-initialised state. Pairs with `omapi-internal.h` row 1. |
| 4 | **C16** `OmPortOpen()` (non-Windows) sets `c_cc[VMIN] = 0`, `c_cc[VTIME] = 1`; `OmPortReadLine()` sleeps 1 ms on the `c <= 0` path | The port is blocking (the preceding `fcntl(fd, F_SETFL, 0)` clears `O_NDELAY`) and upstream never set the timeout values (its own `#warning` asked about them), so `read()` blocked forever on a wedged device and neither `OmPortReadLine()`'s nor `OmCommand()`'s timeout could ever be evaluated — a battery poll from the UI thread beachballed the app. A *removed* device is the opposite case: `read()` fails immediately (EIO/ENXIO) and the retry loop spun a whole core until the caller's timeout. |
| 5 | **C39** The four `DEBUG:` traces around device attach/detach raised from level 0 to level 2 | `om.debug` defaults to 0, so level-0 messages always fire, and `LibOmapiBackend.start()` deliberately routes the log callback to the user-facing Log pane, `--log-file` transcripts and self-test evidence. These were the only unfiltered upstream debug output on a user surface. |
| 6 | **U3** `OmDeviceDiscovery(OM_DEVICE_CONNECTED)` on a device that is *already* CONNECTED: store `OM_DEVICE_REMOVED` and `atomic_thread_fence(memory_order_seq_cst)` before rewriting `port`/`root`/`serialId` | C15's ordering argument covers only REMOVED → CONNECTED. A USB re-enumeration with no intervening `kIOMessageServiceIsTerminated` arrives here still CONNECTED, and those three fields are plain `char[]` rewritten in place, so a reader — in OmGui, a 100 ms tick on the main thread — could read a half-rewritten `root` through `OmGetDevicePath()`/`OmGetDataFilename()`. Taking the device out of CONNECTED first restores the argument for the re-connect case; the fence is needed because a release store orders what precedes it, not what follows. The review's alternative (publish a fresh `OmDeviceState` by swapping the atomic `record->state`) was rejected: the old state can still be in use by a download thread and by any caller holding the pointer, so it could never be freed. The transient window is microseconds and is not a removal, so no `OM_DEVICE_REMOVED` callback is issued. |

## `libomapi/src/omapi-download.c`

| # | What | Why |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **C3**, superseded by **H1/H2/H3** — the shutdown/removal design, described here once. `OmDownloadCancelJoin()` is split into a non-blocking **request** and a bounded **reap**, and there is exactly one authoritative join. `OmDownloadThread()`'s epilogue closes and clears both streams under `om.downloadMutex`, delivers the final status, and then publishes `downloadFinished` as its last act. `OmDownloadRequestCancel()` sets `downloadCancel` and `dup2()`s `/dev/null` over the source descriptor, both under `om.downloadMutex`, and returns. `OmDownloadWaitFinished()` waits on a statically-initialised, never-destroyed mutex/condvar pair for `downloadFinished`. `OmDownloadJoinBounded()` takes the handle, waits within a budget, then joins — or, on timeout, detaches and returns 0, meaning *this state must be leaked and no mutex may be destroyed*. `OmDownloadStartThread()` is the single arming site. `OmBeginDownloadingReference()` reaps a finished-but-unjoined thread before starting a new one, and refuses if the old one is still running. `OmWaitForDownload()` clears `downloadThreadActive` after its join | The contract is: a download thread publishes `downloadFinished` when it has stopped touching its `OmDeviceState`, and nothing frees that state — or destroys a mutex the thread can take — until it has. Everything else follows. **Why not a single cancel+join (C3):** the removal callback runs on the IOKit run-loop thread, where a join is not merely slow but wrong (see `omapi-internal.c` row 2), and `OmShutdown()` runs on `@MainActor`, where an unbounded join on a thread parked in `fread()` on a vanished volume hangs the app — directly after `OmDeviceDiscoveryStop()`'s own up-to-5 s wait. Darwin has no `pthread_timedjoin_np()`, so the bound is on the thread's own publication instead. **Why a separate mutex/condvar:** `om.downloadMutex` is `PTHREAD_MUTEX_RECURSIVE` and waiting on a condition variable with a recursive mutex is undefined; and static initialisation means the protocol survives a shutdown that has given up on a thread — an orphan must still be able to publish, and a mutex destroyed under it would be the very use-after-free this replaces. **Why `dup2()` and not `fclose()`/`close()`:** the copy loop tests `downloadCancel` once per block, so a cancel is only as prompt as the read in flight; replacing the descriptor makes every *subsequent* read report end-of-file without tearing down stdio state another thread owns or freeing a descriptor number that could be reused. It cannot interrupt the read already in flight — which is exactly why the join is bounded as well. Clearing the stream pointers in the epilogue also removes the double `fclose()` a second cancel used to cause. |
| 2 | **C13** `OmGetDataFilename()` builds the path with a bounded `snprintf` into a private `OM_MAX_PATH` buffer, NULL-checks the output buffer, empties it before the lookup, and fails (`OM_E_FAIL`) rather than truncating; `OmReaderOpenDeviceData()`'s buffer is `OM_MAX_PATH` rather than a bare `256` | Upstream `strcat`'d `"/CWA-DATA.CWA"` — 13 bytes — onto a device path that `OmGetDevicePath()` can fill to `OM_MAX_PATH - 1` characters, into a buffer `omapi.h:927` documents as `OM_MAX_PATH` and which all four internal callers here declare as exactly that. Reachability was bounded only by how long the FAT volume label happens to be. The signature is deliberately unchanged (no `OmGetDataFilenameN`): the public header is not touched, and the Swift seam's larger buffer stays valid. |

## `libomapi/src/omapi-testhook.c` (new file, not upstream)

| # | What | Why |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **H1/H3** `OmTestBegin()`/`OmTestEnd()`/`OmTestDeviceCreate()`/`OmTestDownloadStart()` and four observers, all prefixed `OmTest` | The `downloadFinished` contract is the one part of the shutdown redesign that can be exercised with no AX3/AX6 attached, and nothing in the public API can reach it: `OmBeginDownloading()` needs a started library, a discovered device and a seekable file, so it can only ever be handed a source that reads to completion in microseconds. These hooks stand a real `OmDeviceState` up over a caller-supplied descriptor and run the real `OmDownloadThread()` over it through the same `OmDownloadStartThread()`; the test drives `OmDownloadRequestCancel()` and `OmDownloadJoinBounded()` directly — the same functions the removal callback and `OmShutdown()` call. `Tests/OmApiTests/LibOmapiDownloadProtocolTests.swift` binds them with `@_silgen_name`, because `libomapi/include` holds only the public `omapi.h` and that header is deliberately not extended for a test. Nothing in `Sources/` calls any of it. |

## `libomapi/src/omapi-main.c`

| # | What | Why |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **C3**, superseded by **H1/H3/H4** `OmShutdown()` is the one authoritative reap. Two passes: `OmDownloadRequestCancel()` for every device first (so the threads wind down in parallel and share one budget), then `OmDownloadJoinBounded(..., OM_DOWNLOAD_JOIN_TIMEOUT_MS)` per device, freeing a state only when that returns non-zero. `OmDeviceDiscoveryDetached()` is consulted after `OmDeviceDiscoveryStop()`: if the discovery thread was orphaned, *no* state is freed. Either kind of leak skips both `mutex_destroy()` calls | C3 dropped the `OM_DEVICE_CONNECTED` guard (right — it excluded exactly the device that needs cancelling, and the call it guarded was a no-op because `om.initialized` is cleared above), but left the join unbounded on the main thread and still freed the state and destroyed both mutexes afterwards, whatever had happened. Unplug mid-download then Cmd-Q reached that in one step. Leaking a few kilobytes and two mutexes on a quit that was already going wrong beats `free()`ing memory under a live `fread()` and destroying a mutex a live thread is locking. See `omapi-download.c` row 1 and `omapi-devicefinder-mac.c` row 14. |

| 2 | **H1/H3** `OmStartup()` skips both `mutex_init()` calls if an earlier `OmShutdown()` had to leak | That shutdown skipped `mutex_destroy()` precisely because an orphaned thread can still lock the pair; re-initialising a mutex another thread may hold is the same undefined behaviour. The existing pair is reused. |

## `libomapi/src/omapi-status.c`

| # | What | Why |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **C38** `OmCommand()`: the FW-40 `"COMMIT"` special case is guarded with `expected != NULL` | It `strcmp`'d `expected` twenty lines before the function's own `if (expected == NULL)` check, and `omapi.h` documents the parameter as optional. Latent — no current caller passes NULL — but `OmCommand()` is public API one thin Swift wrapper away. |

## `libomapi/src/omapi-reader.c`

| # | What | Why |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **C37** `OmReaderNextBlock()` rejects a block (`return 0`) whose axis count is zero, and one whose sample-rate code is 0–3; the sample-rate computation moved above the sample unpacking so the rejection happens first | `(512 - 32) / (numAxes * 2)` and the block-timing divisions by `3200 / (1 << (15 - rateCode))` both divide by a value taken straight from the packet. Zero axes, and every rate code below 4 (whose true rate is under 1 Hz and so truncates to zero), made the divisor zero. arm64's UDIV/SDIV return 0 instead of trapping, so instead of crashing, upstream produced a zero-duration block with a zero rate that `DataLevel.add`'s `guard interval > 0` silently dropped — whole regions of a partly-corrupt file plotted as missing with no diagnostic. Still undefined behaviour. Guarded by `Tests/OmApiTests/OmReaderBlockGuardTests.swift`. |

## `omconvert/`, `cwa-convert/`

No source modifications. Files excluded from vendoring are listed in each `UPSTREAM.md`.
